cornerCallouts: Here they come into Variante del Rettifilo, the first chicane. A crucial braking zone.
Now it's on to the Curva Grande, a high-speed sweeper that demands commitment.
Next up, the Variante della Roggia, another tricky chicane requiring pinpoint accuracy.
Drivers are flat out through the Curva di Lesmo, a deceptively challenging corner.
Through Lesmo 2, carrying as much speed as possible to set up the next straight.
Approaching the Variante Ascari, a complex sequence of corners that separates the good from the great.
Now, they're powering down the straight towards the Curva Parabolica, that iconic final corner.
Exiting Parabolica, it's a drag race to the finish line. Who will have the traction?
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this Short layout. The high-speed nature of Monza always punishes the rubber.
With the shorter lap, the pit window is going to be tighter than usual. Every second counts in the pit lane.
Fuel consumption will be critical. Managing the fuel load will be key to a strong finish.
The slipstream will be powerful here. Expect plenty of overtaking opportunities down the straights.
The balance between top speed and downforce will be crucial. Finding the right compromise is the key to success.
A well-timed safety car could completely change the complexion of the race. Strategy teams need to be ready to react.
With the shortened layout, traffic management will be even more important. Navigating the backmarkers cleanly will be essential.
The undercut could be particularly powerful here, as the shorter lap means less time lost in the pit lane.
weatherCommentary: The mountains surrounding Monza can create unpredictable weather patterns. Keep an eye on those radar screens.
The heat radiating off the asphalt is intense. This will affect tire performance and driver stamina.
A sudden downpour could turn this race on its head. The low grip levels at Monza are treacherous in the wet.
The wind direction can have a significant impact on aerodynamic performance, especially down the main straight.
That cloud cover could bring cooler temperatures, which would benefit some teams more than others.
